text.p: Campbell Soup Co. said Monday it was reviewing non-core operations with annual sales of $1.4 billion as part of a strategy to focus on its core businesses.

But the Camden, N.J.-based giant soup maker has made no decisions on whether to sell any or all of the units, which it declined to identify. Spokesman Leonard Griehs said analysts were informed of the review at a meeting Friday.
The review does not include core businesses, which generate $6.1 billion in annual sales, or operations with $500 million in revenues that have already been targeted for sale, Griehs said.
"There is an additional $1.4 billion in sales that we're generating that we would consider as less-strategic businesses, or non-strategic businesses," he said.
"We're evaluating currently what's the best strategy to create the most wealth for our shareowners from the current portfolio of businesses that we have," he said.
Campbell's core businesses are soups, sauces, bakery and biscuits, and food service, he said.
Analysts have speculated that Campbell may sell its Swanson frozen foods and Vlasic pickles lines, among others.

Nesbitt Burns analyst Ellen Baras said Swanson's would be a more likely target than market-leader Vlasic. Outside of food-giant ConAgra Inc., there were few obvious potential buyers, she said. But a small group such as one led by the operations management could be a candidate, she added.
Griehs said Campbell has not discussed a timetable for the evaluation. "We'll provide further updates in the near-term," he said.
Campbell has been selling off non-core assets over the last several years.
In announcing a restructuring and stock buyback in September, the company said it would sell several businesses, with sales of about $500 million, over a two-year period.
The company said in May it had sold its Marie's salad dressing line and its poultry operations.
Campbell stock rose $1.94 to $50.875 in afternoon composite trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
